efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-01.question: In Ephesians 1:3, God has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in Christ.
efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-01.feedbackCorrect: It is the praise that opens the letter: every blessing comes in Christ.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Ephesians 1:3: God has blessed us with every spiritual blessing.

efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-01.hint: Read the beginning of Paul's praise.

efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-02.question: In Ephesians 1:4, tap when God chose us in him.
efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-02.feedbackCorrect: The choice is presented as coming before the world itself.

feedbackWrong.a: That tells the way of the holy life, not the moment of the choice.
feedbackWrong.b: That tells before whom we will be holy, not when we were chosen.

efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-02.hint: Look for the expression of time in the verse.

efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-03.question: According to Ephesians 1:7, what do we have in him?
efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-03.feedbackCorrect: In him we have redemption through his blood and forgiveness of sins.

feedbackWrong.a: The text speaks of redemption from sins, not of riches.
feedbackWrong.c: The verse does not promise the absence of suffering.
feedbackWrong.d: Redemption comes through Christ's blood, not through our works.

efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-03.hint: Read what we receive through his blood.

options.c: Freedom from all suffering

efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-04.question: Put Ephesians 1:3 in the order of the text.
efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-04.feedbackCorrect: The praise goes from God the Father to the blessings given in Christ.

feedbackWrong.default: Start by blessing God the Father and end in Christ.

efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-04.hint: The verse begins with praise to God.

efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-05.question: In Ephesians 1:5, what did God predestine us for?
efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-05.feedbackCorrect: God predestined us to be his children through Christ.

feedbackWrong.a: God brings us near as children; he does not keep us apart.
feedbackWrong.c: The destiny mentioned is the opposite: being welcomed as children.

efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-05.hint: See the destiny God gave us as a family.

efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-06.question: What does Ephesians 1:3 say that connects to this context?
efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-06.feedbackCorrect: Paul says God has already blessed us with every blessing in Christ.

feedbackWrong.b: The verb is in the past: God has already blessed us in Christ.
feedbackWrong.c: The blessing is given in Christ, not bought by our merit.

efesios-sem-ef-01-bencaos-06.hint: See what God has already blessed us with.

options.c: Blessings by our merit

efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-01.question: In Ephesians 1:4–5, being chosen in Christ goes together with being made a child of God.
efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-01.feedbackCorrect: Choice and adoption appear together, tied to Christ.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread both verses: choice and adoption come together.

efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-01.hint: Read the two verses as a single sentence.

efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-02.question: In Ephesians 1:4, tap the word that shows the purpose of the choice.
efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-02.feedbackCorrect: The choice has a goal: a holy life before God.

feedbackWrong.b: That links the verse to the earlier praise; it does not show the goal.
feedbackWrong.c: That tells in whom we were chosen, not the purpose.

efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-02.hint: Look at the link between choice and holiness.

efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-03.question: How does Ephesians 1:5 explain adoption as children?
efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-03.feedbackCorrect: Adoption comes through Jesus Christ, according to God's will.

feedbackWrong.a: The text speaks of being made children, not of separating believers.
feedbackWrong.c: The text places the initiative in God's will, not in effort.
feedbackWrong.d: Adoption comes first, as a gift, not as a final prize.

efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-03.hint: See through whom and according to whom it happens.

options.a: It separates the children from other believers
options.b: It happens through Christ, by God's will
options.c: It depends first on each person's effort
options.d: It is a prize for those who already live without failure

efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-04.question: How does the praise advance in Ephesians 1:3–4?
efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-04.feedbackCorrect: From the blessing in Christ, the text returns to the choice and its holy goal.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the blessing in Christ and end with the holy goal.

efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-04.hint: A holy life is the point of arrival.

options.b: God chooses before the world existed
options.c: The goal is a holy life in love

efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-05.question: In Ephesians 1:6, how did God grant us his grace in the Beloved?
efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-05.feedbackCorrect: Grace in the Beloved is a gift, granted without charge.

feedbackWrong.a: Grace is granted freely, not in measured portions.
feedbackWrong.c: The text highlights that it is free, not that grace is rare.

efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-06.question: What connects Ephesians 1:7 to Colossians 1:14?
efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, in Christ there is redemption and forgiveness of sins.

feedbackWrong.a: Redemption is his, through his blood; it is not bought by us.
feedbackWrong.c: Both texts speak of forgiven sins, not of suffering.

efesios-cam-ef-01-bencaos-06.hint: Compare what we receive in him in both texts.

options.c: The end of all suffering now

efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-01.question: In Ephesians 1:3, spiritual blessings depend first on what we manage to do for God.
efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-01.feedbackCorrect: The text presents the blessing as already given by God in Christ.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the verse: God is the one who blesses, and the place is in Christ.

efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-01.hint: See who the subject of the action is in the verse.

efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-02.question: In Ephesians 1:7, tap the phrase that shows forgiveness has a price paid by Christ.
efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-02.feedbackCorrect: Redemption is through Christ's blood, not through our payment.

feedbackWrong.b: Grace shows God's riches, not the means of payment.
feedbackWrong.c: Sins are what is forgiven, not the means of redemption.

efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-02.hint: Look for the means by which we have redemption.

efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-03.question: What reading of Ephesians 1:4 does the text support about being chosen in Christ?
efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-03.feedbackCorrect: The verse itself links the choice to the goal of a holy life.

feedbackWrong.b: The choice comes before the world, not as a final reward.
feedbackWrong.c: The stated goal is precisely that we be holy before him.
feedbackWrong.d: Paul writes to the saints in Ephesus, not only to leaders.

efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-03.hint: Read to the end of the verse and see the goal.

options.a: The choice points to holiness lived out in love
options.b: The choice is a reward for a perfect life
options.c: The choice makes a holy life unnecessary
options.d: The choice applies only to church leaders

efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-04.question: Which sequence reveals the path of sonship that begins in Ephesians 1:5?
efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-04.feedbackCorrect: God makes us children in Christ, and the Spirit confirms that sonship.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with God's action in Ephesians and end with the Spirit.

efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-04.hint: Follow from Ephesians to John and then Romans.

options.a: God makes us children through Christ
options.b: Whoever receives Christ becomes a child of God
options.c: We receive the Spirit who cries Abba, Father

efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-05.question: In Ephesians 1:7, which word names the deliverance we have in him?
efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-05.feedbackCorrect: In Christ we have the deliverance paid for by his blood.

feedbackWrong.b: The text announces deliverance, not condemnation, for those in him.
feedbackWrong.c: Christ brings us near to God; he does not keep us apart.

efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-05.hint: It is the term linked to Christ's blood.

efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-06.question: What connects Ephesians 1:5 to Romans 8:15?
efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-06.feedbackCorrect: Made children, we receive the Spirit by whom we cry Father.

feedbackWrong.a: Sonship here is adoption by God, not natural birth.
feedbackWrong.c: Romans says we did not receive a spirit of fear, but of adoption.

efesios-pro-ef-01-bencaos-06.hint: See what the Spirit leads us to call God.

options.c: Children who live in fear

efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-01.question: In Ephesians 2:8, we are saved by grace through faith.
efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-01.feedbackCorrect: Salvation is by grace, received through faith.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Ephesians 2:8: by grace you have been saved, through faith.

efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-01.hint: Read the first part of the verse.

efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-02.question: In Ephesians 2:5, tap how we were before God gave us life.
efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-02.feedbackCorrect: Our state was death in transgressions, until God acted.

feedbackWrong.a: That tells with whom God gave us life, not our state before.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the result of grace, not our earlier state.

efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-02.hint: See our state before God's action.

efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-03.question: According to Ephesians 2:9, salvation is not the result of what?
efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-03.feedbackCorrect: It is not by works, so that no one may boast in themselves.

feedbackWrong.a: Faith is the means of receiving, not what the text denies here.
feedbackWrong.b: The verse denies works as a basis; it does not speak of prayer.
feedbackWrong.d: Grace is precisely the source of salvation in 2:8.

efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-03.hint: Read the word right after result.

options.c: Works

efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-04.question: Put Ephesians 2:8 in the order of the text.
efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-04.feedbackCorrect: Grace, faith and gift appear in that order in the verse.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with grace and end with the gift of God.

efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-04.hint: The verse ends by saying what salvation is.

efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-05.question: In Ephesians 2:10, what does Paul say we are of God?
efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-05.feedbackCorrect: We are God's workmanship, created in Christ for good works.

feedbackWrong.a: God is the one who makes; we are what he made, not his owners.
feedbackWrong.b: The text makes us his workmanship, not his judges.

efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-05.hint: See how God made us in Christ.

efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-06.question: What does Ephesians 2:8 say that connects to this context?
efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-06.feedbackCorrect: Salvation is God's gift, received, and not a wage paid.

feedbackWrong.b: The text calls salvation a gift, not something deserved.
feedbackWrong.c: Ephesians 2:9 denies that it is the result of works.

efesios-sem-ef-02-graca-06.hint: See where salvation comes from in the text.

options.c: Salvation bought with works

efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-01.question: In Ephesians 2:10, good works come before grace and serve to buy salvation.
efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-01.feedbackCorrect: Good works are the goal of those whom God has already recreated in Christ.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the order: first God creates us in Christ, then come the works.

efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-01.hint: Notice the order between being created and doing works.

efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-02.question: In Ephesians 2:8, tap the word that opens the explanation of what was said.
efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-02.feedbackCorrect: The opening word explains why the readers are alive in Christ.

feedbackWrong.a: That shows the means, but it comes after the opening.
feedbackWrong.c: That names who is saved, not what opens the explanation.

efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-02.hint: Look at the first word of the verse.

efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-03.question: How does Ephesians 2:9 relate to Ephesians 2:8?
efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-03.feedbackCorrect: After the gift, Paul closes the door to pride in works.

feedbackWrong.a: Grace reaches those who were dead, not only those who did good.
feedbackWrong.b: The text denies works as a result that produces salvation.
feedbackWrong.c: The basis remains grace received through faith.

efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-03.hint: See what the second verse denies.

options.a: It limits grace to those who have already done good
options.b: It says human effort is the means of salvation
options.c: It swaps faith for works as the basis of salvation
options.d: It reinforces that no one can exalt themselves by their own effort

efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-04.question: How does God's action advance in Ephesians 2:5–6?
efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-04.feedbackCorrect: From dead, we are made alive and seated with Christ.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the state of death and end with Christ in the heavens.

efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-04.hint: The end is with Christ, in the heavenly places.

options.c: Seated in the heavenly places

efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-05.question: In Ephesians 2:9, who can boast because of works?
efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-05.feedbackCorrect: If salvation is a gift, what is left is gratitude, not self-glory.

feedbackWrong.b: The text closes the door to anyone's pride.
feedbackWrong.c: That is a word of time; it does not answer who boasts.

efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-05.hint: See who is left with no reason for pride.

efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-06.question: What connects Ephesians 2:8 to Romans 6:23?
efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, what God gives is a gift, not a wage.

feedbackWrong.a: Ephesians states that salvation does not come from us.
feedbackWrong.c: Romans calls sin the wage; life is a free gift.

efesios-cam-ef-02-graca-06.hint: Compare what God gives in both texts.

options.c: Life as a deserved wage

efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-01.question: In Ephesians 2:12, even without Christ the Gentiles had hope and God in the world.
efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-01.feedbackCorrect: The text describes that time as without Christ and without hope.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the end of the verse: without hope and without God in the world.

efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-01.hint: Read the description of that time to the end.

efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-02.question: In Ephesians 2:10, tap the phrase that shows what we were created in Christ for.
efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-02.feedbackCorrect: Recreated in Christ, our goal is the good works prepared.

feedbackWrong.b: That tells when God prepared, not the goal of the creation.
feedbackWrong.c: That tells what we are of God, not what we were created for.

efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-02.hint: Look for the goal of the new creation in Christ.

efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-03.question: What reading of Ephesians 2:8–10 does the text support about good works?
efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-03.feedbackCorrect: Works come after the new creation, as its fruit.

feedbackWrong.a: Salvation is a gift before works, not payment for them.
feedbackWrong.c: It is grace that recreates us precisely for these works.
feedbackWrong.d: The text ties works to God's plan, not to vanity.

efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-03.hint: Notice the order of the three verses.

options.a: They are the payment that buys salvation
options.b: They are the fruit of those whom God has already recreated in Christ
options.c: They make grace unnecessary for living
options.d: They serve to show superiority over others

efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Ephesians 2:5?
efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-04.feedbackCorrect: Life given, salvation received as a gift, and a new life in works.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with life given to the dead and end with works.

efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-04.hint: Follow the order of Ephesians 2, from verse 5 to 10.

options.a: God gives life to those who were dead
options.b: Salvation is received as a gift through faith
options.c: The saved live in the good works prepared

efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-05.question: In Ephesians 2:8, through what are we saved by grace?
efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-05.feedbackCorrect: Grace is received through trust in God.

feedbackWrong.a: The means named in the text is not the law, but trust.
feedbackWrong.c: Works are denied as a basis in the next verse.

efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-05.hint: See the means the text points to.

efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-06.question: What connects Ephesians 2:9 to Titus 3:5?
efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, God saves by mercy, not by works.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts deny works as the basis of salvation.
feedbackWrong.c: Neither text speaks of deserving more than others.

efesios-pro-ef-02-graca-06.hint: Compare the basis of salvation in both texts.

options.c: Saved by deserving more

efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-01.question: In Ephesians 6:11, we are to put on the full armor of God in order to stand firm.
efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-01.feedbackCorrect: The text commands us to take the whole armor in order to stand firm.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Ephesians 6:11: put on the full armor of God.

efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-01.hint: Read the command Paul gives in the verse.

efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-02.question: In Ephesians 6:14, tap the first piece named for standing firm.
efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-02.feedbackCorrect: The first piece named is girding yourself with truth.

feedbackWrong.a: Righteousness describes the breastplate, named after truth.
feedbackWrong.b: The breastplate is named right after, as the piece you put on.

efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-02.hint: Read the beginning of the final command.

efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-03.question: According to Ephesians 6:12, against whom is our struggle not?
efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-03.feedbackCorrect: The struggle is not against people, but against spiritual forces.

feedbackWrong.a: These rulers are also named in the struggle.
feedbackWrong.c: The text names these forces as the side of the struggle.
feedbackWrong.d: Against these, yes, the text says we struggle.

efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-03.hint: Read the first part of the verse.

options.c: Spiritual forces of evil

efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-04.question: Put Ephesians 6:11 in the order of the text.
efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-04.feedbackCorrect: Putting on the armor comes before the goal of standing firm.

feedbackWrong.default: Start by putting on the armor and end with the schemes.

efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-04.hint: The verse begins with the command to put on.

efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-05.question: In Ephesians 6:10, whose strength do we draw on to be strong?
efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-05.feedbackCorrect: We are strengthened in the Lord and in the strength of his power.

feedbackWrong.b: Fear is not a source of strength mentioned by Paul here.
feedbackWrong.c: The text points to the Lord's power, not our effort.

efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-05.hint: See whom the strength belongs to.

efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-06.question: What does Ephesians 6:10 say that connects to this context?
efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-06.feedbackCorrect: Paul tells us to seek in the Lord the strength to stand firm.

feedbackWrong.a: The text puts the source in the Lord and his power.
feedbackWrong.b: Firmness here depends on the Lord; it does not do without God.

efesios-sem-ef-03-igreja-06.hint: See where Paul tells us to seek strength.

options.c: Strength received from the Lord

efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-01.question: In Ephesians 6:12, Paul says our main struggle is against people of flesh and blood.
efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-01.feedbackCorrect: Paul denies exactly that and points to spiritual forces.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the beginning of the verse: we do not struggle against flesh and blood.

efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-01.hint: Read the first statement of the verse.

efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-02.question: In Ephesians 6:12, tap the word that explains why we put on the armor.
efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-02.feedbackCorrect: The explanation begins by showing the struggle is not against people.

feedbackWrong.a: That tells what we do; it does not open the verse's explanation.
feedbackWrong.b: That indicates opposition, but it comes after the opening.

efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-02.hint: Look at the first word of the verse.

efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-03.question: How does Ephesians 6:11 relate to Ephesians 6:10?
efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-03.feedbackCorrect: First the source of strength, then the way to stand firm.

feedbackWrong.a: The armor comes precisely from God, the source of strength.
feedbackWrong.c: The next verse denies a struggle against people.
feedbackWrong.d: The text joins depending on the Lord with putting on the armor.

efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-03.hint: Read the two verses in sequence.

options.a: The armor replaces the need to depend on the Lord
options.b: Putting on the armor is the concrete way of seeking strength in the Lord
options.c: Putting on the armor serves to defeat people
options.d: The Lord's strength makes any preparation of ours unnecessary

efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-04.question: How does the command advance in Ephesians 6:12–13?
efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-04.feedbackCorrect: Once the struggle is understood, we take the armor to resist and stand firm.

feedbackWrong.default: Start by understanding the struggle and end by standing firm.

efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-04.hint: Standing firm is the point of arrival.

options.a: Understand that the struggle is not against people
options.b: Take the full armor of God
options.c: Resist in the evil day and stand firm

efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-05.question: In Ephesians 6:13, what does the armor help us do in the evil day?
efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-05.feedbackCorrect: With the armor, we resist in the evil day and stand firm.

feedbackWrong.b: The stated goal is to resist and stand, not to attack people.
feedbackWrong.c: The text speaks of standing firm, not of fleeing the struggle.

efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-05.hint: See the goal of taking the armor.

efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-06.question: What connects Ephesians 6:11 to Romans 13:12?
efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, God calls his people to put on.

feedbackWrong.a: Ephesians denies that the struggle is against people.
feedbackWrong.c: The weapons come from God and from the light, not from ourselves.

efesios-cam-ef-03-igreja-06.hint: Compare the verb both texts use.

options.c: Trusting our own weapons

efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-01.question: In Ephesians 6:13, taking the armor aims at resisting in the evil day and standing firm.
efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-01.feedbackCorrect: The stated goal is to resist in the evil day and stand firm.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the verse: the goal is to resist and stand firm.

efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-01.hint: Read the purpose of taking the armor.

efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-02.question: In Ephesians 6:9, tap the phrase that shows God treats everyone without favoritism.
efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-02.feedbackCorrect: Before the Lord, servant and master stand on the same ground.

feedbackWrong.a: That says where the Lord is, not how he treats everyone.
feedbackWrong.c: That speaks of giving up threats, not of God's equal treatment.

efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-02.hint: Look for how the Lord treats servant and master.

efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-03.question: What reading of Ephesians 6:12 does the text support about the believer's struggle?
efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-03.feedbackCorrect: The text takes people off the target and names spiritual forces.

feedbackWrong.a: The strength asked for is in the Lord, not in the body or courage.
feedbackWrong.b: Attacking people contradicts the denial that opens the verse.
feedbackWrong.c: The text denies precisely that people are the target of the struggle.

efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-03.hint: Start with what the verse denies.

options.a: It is won only with physical strength and courage
options.b: It requires attacking people to defend the faith
options.c: It is against anyone who gets in our way
options.d: It is not against people, but of a spiritual order

efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-04.question: Which sequence reveals the putting on that begins in Ephesians 6:14?
efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-04.feedbackCorrect: Paul uses the same image of putting on pieces in order to stand firm.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with truth in Ephesians and follow to the pieces in Thessalonians.

efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-04.hint: Follow from Ephesians to First Thessalonians.

options.b: Put on the breastplate of faith and love
options.c: Take the helmet of the hope of salvation

efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-05.question: In Ephesians 6:14, what is the breastplate made of, according to Paul's image?
efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-05.feedbackCorrect: The breastplate named in the text is that of righteousness.

feedbackWrong.a: The piece named protects with righteousness, not with vengeance.
feedbackWrong.c: The text names a character, not an outward appearance.

efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-05.hint: It is the second piece named in the verse.

efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-06.question: What connects Ephesians 6:14 to 1 Thessalonians 5:8?
efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, putting on the pieces sustains a firm life.

feedbackWrong.a: In both texts, putting on has a real function of firmness.
feedbackWrong.b: The pieces are gifts tied to God, not isolated effort.

efesios-pro-ef-03-igreja-06.hint: Compare the pieces both texts tell us to put on.

options.c: Clothed to stand firm

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-01.question: In Ephesians 1:7, we have redemption through our good works and not through Christ's blood.
efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-01.feedbackCorrect: Redemption is through Christ's blood, according to God's grace.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the verse: redemption is through his blood.

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-01.hint: Read the means by which we have redemption.

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-02.question: In Ephesians 1:3, tap the place named at the end of the verse.
efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-02.feedbackCorrect: The spiritual blessings are in the heavenly places in Christ.

feedbackWrong.a: That names Jesus, not the place named at the end.
feedbackWrong.c: That opens the praise; it does not name the place of the blessings.

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-02.hint: Go to the final part of the verse.

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-03.question: According to Ephesians 2:9, salvation is not the result of what?
efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-03.feedbackCorrect: It is not by works, so that no one may boast in themselves.

feedbackWrong.b: Faith is the means of receiving, not what the text denies.
feedbackWrong.c: The verse denies works as a basis; it does not speak of prayer.
feedbackWrong.d: Grace is precisely the source of salvation in 2:8.

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-03.hint: Read the word right after result.

options.c: Prayer

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-04.question: Put Ephesians 6:14 in the order of the text.
efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-04.feedbackCorrect: Stand firm, gird yourself with truth and put on the breastplate.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the command to stand firm and end with the breastplate.

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-04.hint: The verse begins with the posture of firmness.

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-05.question: In Ephesians 1:5, God predestined us for the adoption of whom?
efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-05.feedbackCorrect: God predestined us to be welcomed as children.

feedbackWrong.b: The destiny named is sonship, not only service.
feedbackWrong.c: Adoption brings us near; it does not keep us strangers to God.

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-05.hint: See who becomes part of the family.

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-06.question: What does Ephesians 1:3 say that connects to this context?
efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-06.feedbackCorrect: Paul says God has already blessed us with every blessing in Christ.

feedbackWrong.a: The text speaks of spiritual blessing, not only material goods.
feedbackWrong.c: The blessing is given in Christ, not bought by merit.

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-06.hint: See what God blessed us with.

options.c: Blessing by our merit

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-07.question: In Ephesians 6:12, tap a spiritual power named in the struggle.
efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-07.feedbackCorrect: The principalities are named among the powers of the struggle.

feedbackWrong.a: Flesh is also part of what the text denies as the target.
feedbackWrong.b: Blood is part of the expression the text denies as the target.

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-07.hint: Read the part after the initial denial.

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-08.question: Put Ephesians 2:8 in the order of the text.
efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-08.feedbackCorrect: Grace, faith and gift appear in that order in the verse.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with grace and end with the gift of God.

efesios-sem-ef-04-desafio-08.hint: The verse ends by saying what salvation is.

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-01.question: In Ephesians 2:5–6, God gave us life and raised us together with Christ.
efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-01.feedbackCorrect: Dead, we were made alive and raised with Christ.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the verses: God gave us life together with Christ.

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-01.hint: Read the two verses as a single action.

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-02.question: In Ephesians 6:13, tap the word that draws the conclusion from the previous verse.
efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-02.feedbackCorrect: From the nature of the struggle, Paul concludes that we must take the armor.

feedbackWrong.b: That is the command that comes after the conclusion drawn.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the final goal: standing in the evil day.

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-02.hint: Look at the first word of the verse.

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-03.question: How does Ephesians 1:5 connect to Ephesians 1:4?
efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-03.feedbackCorrect: Chosen in Christ, we are also made children of God.

feedbackWrong.b: The choice already carries the goal of a holy life in 1:4.
feedbackWrong.c: Sonship is given by God in Christ, not earned.
feedbackWrong.d: Paul writes to believers in Ephesus, made children in Christ.

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-03.hint: Read the two verses in sequence.

options.a: Being chosen in Christ leads to the sonship God gives
options.b: Sonship cancels the call to a holy life
options.c: The choice depends on the sonship we earn
options.d: Sonship applies only to those born in Israel

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-04.question: How does God's action advance in Ephesians 2:5–6?
efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-04.feedbackCorrect: From dead, we are made alive and seated with Christ.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the state of death and end with Christ in the heavens.

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-04.hint: The end is with Christ, in the heavenly places.

options.c: Seated in the heavenly places

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-05.question: In Ephesians 6:11, how are we to stand against the devil's schemes?
efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-05.feedbackCorrect: With the armor on, the goal is to stand firm against the schemes.

feedbackWrong.a: Being ready helps, but the word cited is another posture.
feedbackWrong.c: The word in the text describes the posture of one who does not give way.

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-05.hint: See the goal of putting on the armor.

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-06.question: What connects Ephesians 2:10 to Titus 2:14?
efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-06.feedbackCorrect: Recreated in Christ, we are a people devoted to good works.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts expect good works from those who have been saved.
feedbackWrong.c: Works are the fruit of salvation, not its price.

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-06.hint: Compare God's goal in both texts.

options.b: Created and zealous for good works
options.c: Works that buy salvation

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-07.question: In Ephesians 2:8, tap the word that opens the explanation of salvation.
efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-07.feedbackCorrect: The opening word explains the new life given with Christ.

feedbackWrong.b: That shows the means, but it comes after the opening.
feedbackWrong.c: That names who is saved, not what opens the explanation.

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-07.hint: Look at the first word of the verse.

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-08.question: How do the great themes of Ephesians link together?
efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-08.feedbackCorrect: Blessing in Christ, salvation as a gift and a firm life in the armor.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the letter, from the opening blessing to the final armor.

efesios-cam-ef-04-desafio-08.hint: Follow the order of the letter, from beginning to end.

options.c: A firm life with the armor

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-01.question: In Ephesians 6:12, the armor serves mainly to defeat people who do us harm.
efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-01.feedbackCorrect: The text denies people as the target and names spiritual forces.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the verse: we do not struggle against flesh and blood.

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-01.hint: Read the first statement of the verse.

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-02.question: In Ephesians 1:6, tap how God granted us his grace.
efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-02.feedbackCorrect: Grace in the Beloved is granted freely, without charge.

feedbackWrong.a: The Beloved is the one in whom we receive, not the manner of grace.
feedbackWrong.b: Glory is the praise that results, not the manner of granting.

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-02.hint: See in what manner grace came.

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-03.question: What reading of Ephesians 2:8–9 does the text support about salvation?
efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-03.feedbackCorrect: Salvation is God's gift, received by faith, and not a wage.

feedbackWrong.a: Faith receives the gift; it is not a currency to outdo others.
feedbackWrong.b: It reaches those who were dead, not only those who never fail.
feedbackWrong.d: The text calls the opposite a wage; here salvation is a gift.

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-03.hint: Put the two verses together and see the basis.

options.a: It is the achievement of those with more faith than others
options.b: It is a prize for those who never fail God
options.c: It is a gift received by faith, with no basis in works
options.d: It is a wage paid to those who do good works

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-04.question: Which sequence reveals the path that begins in Ephesians 1:7?
efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-04.feedbackCorrect: Forgiven in Christ, we receive life and walk in good works.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with redemption and end with the good works prepared.

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-04.hint: The good works are the point of arrival.

options.b: Life received as a free gift
options.c: Good works prepared to walk in

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-05.question: In Ephesians 6:14, what is the first piece of armor named?
efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-05.feedbackCorrect: The first piece named is girding yourself with truth.

feedbackWrong.a: Strength comes from the Lord in 6:10; the piece here is another.
feedbackWrong.b: Courage is not the piece named in this verse.

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-05.hint: It is the piece mentioned before the breastplate.

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-06.question: What connects Ephesians 6:11 to 1 Thessalonians 5:8?
efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, putting on the pieces sustains a firm life.

feedbackWrong.a: The pieces are tied to God, not made by ourselves.
feedbackWrong.b: Ephesians denies flesh and blood as the target of the struggle.

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-06.hint: Compare what both texts tell us to put on.

options.c: Clothed to stand in the day

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-07.question: In Ephesians 2:10, tap the phrase that shows good works were already prepared by God.
efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-07.feedbackCorrect: The good works were prepared by God before we walked in them.

feedbackWrong.a: That says where we were created, not the preparation of the works.
feedbackWrong.c: That says what we are of God, not when he prepared.

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-07.hint: Look for when God prepared these works.

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-08.question: Which sequence reveals the goal that begins in Ephesians 6:13?
efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-08.feedbackCorrect: Take the armor, resist in the evil day and stand firm.

feedbackWrong.default: Start by taking the armor and end by standing firm.

efesios-pro-ef-04-desafio-08.hint: Standing firm is the point of arrival.

options.a: Take the full armor of God
options.c: Stand firm after having done everything
